title: Human-Checkpointed Micro-Experiment Orchestration (WIP)
content:
Purpose
This doc captures a practical playbook for coordinating small-scope experiments (micro-experiments) where an automated rollout is intentionally gated by a human checkpoint. Goal is to reduce blast radius for risky LLM behavior changes while keeping fast iteration velocity.

Scope and assumptions
- Applies to cross-functional rollouts touching hosted, dedicated, and private deployment modes.
- Focused on feature changes that modify model selection, prompt templates, reranking heuristics, or output formatting logic (i.e., any change that can alter user-facing text).
- Not intended for infra-only changes (scaling, autoscaler tuning) except where they interact with traffic partitioning.

Why a human checkpoint?
- Some regressions are subtle: safety edge cases, hallucination patterns, brand tone shifts. Automating detection for all such cases is brittle.
- A short manual review step (3–30 minutes) in the exposure path allows product + ML + SRE to validate signals before widening blast radius.
- Checkpoint remains auditable and reproducible via recorded artifacts.

Owners and roles (minimal RACI)
- Experiment Owner (EO): product manager or solutions engineer; owns hypothesis and release criteria.
- Model Steward (MS): applied-ml engineer; validates model variant/quantization assumptions and known-failure modes.
- Observation Steward (OS): observability/console owner; ensures dashboards and signal health.
- Oncall Lead (OL): SRE or incident lead; responsible for rollback on signal trigger.
- Human Gate Approver (HGA): cross-functional person (rotation between EO/MS/OS) who signs off.

Naming and metadata conventions (helps automation)
- Experiment id: team_short/yyqX/shortname (e.g., console/25q1/chef-rlhf-guardrail)
- Short description: 1-line goal (intent + expected measurable change)
- Safety category tag: e.g., hallucination, toxicity, data-exposure, formatting
- Baseline model tag and candidate model tag(s)
- Traffic partitioning config (percent, cohorts) embedded in rollout descriptor

Experiment lifecycle (recommended fast-path)
1) Preflight (2–3 days or less for small experiments)
   - EO writes hypothesis, expected quant metrics, and known risk vectors. Attach 50–200 prompt examples used for regression testing.
   - MS validates model variant and quantization profile; notes any architecture caveats.
   - OS wires up lightweight dashboard: latency, p50/p95 token cost, failure rates, top error classes, slice-level quality metrics (per prompt group), and cohort conversion delta if applicable.

2) Pilot (internal-only traffic, 0.1–1%)
   - Short-run (4–24 hours) to catch immediate regressions. Collect qualitative examples in a shared doc and tag interesting failures.
   - If catastrophic (safety, PII leak), immediate rollback and incident stand-up.

3) Human-Checkpointed Canary (HC-Canary) (1–10% but gated)
   - Deploy to a small external slice (e.g., 2% of traffic or 5% of a low-risk region).
   - Rollout automation pauses after initial traffic ramp and notifies HGA via Slack/console.
   - HGA performs a checklist review (see checklist) and either approves or aborts widening.

4) Gradual expansion (automated)
   - After gate approval, automated ramping continues per policies (e.g., double every 2 hours while passing signal checks).

5) Post-mortem and artifactization
   - Every HC-Canary must publish a 1–page outcome: what changed, quantitative deltas, anomalies found, and long-term action items (tune prompt, add evals, model revert).

Human gate checklist (quick, intended for 5–20 minutes)
- Telemetry quick-glance: overall error rate, latency drift (>30% p95?), token-cost delta per call (>20%?)
- Safety slices: flagged content increase? new NER/PII leak examples? top 10 worst-scoring prompts compared to baseline
- Quality checks: NPS/CTR proxies if available, and manual read of 20 representative outputs across cohorts
- Resource/ops: any node/pod/orchestration alerts? queueing/backpressure?
- Cost: estimated 24h spend delta on this slice (rough estimate)
- Stakeholder greenlight: PM, MS, and OL must sign-off (via Slack reaction or console button)

Automatic signal thresholds (fast rejects)
- Safety threshold: >3 PII-exposure incidents within 1h OR any single high-severity policy-trigger -> auto-abort
- Latency: p95 spike >2x baseline sustained for 10m -> auto-throttle to lower capacity
- Error rate: 5xx or model-fallback triggers >1.5x baseline for 15m -> auto-revert
- Quality regression: drop in eval pass-rate for critical prompt-set >7% -> pause and notify EO

Escalation flow (when human gate aborts or auto-abort triggers)
- Automated page to OL (pagerduty) + Slack channel #hc-canary-{experiment}
- EO assembles a 30-minute triage call; immediate revert if root cause unknown and impact >user-visible threshold
- If revert not possible, apply traffic-split fallback to baseline model and open an incident ticket (JIRA)

Observability recommendations (quick list)
- Dashboard: baseline vs experiment overlay with configurable rolling window (15m/1h/24h)
- Top-k example sampling: surface worst outputs and their inputs side-by-side
- Slice telemetry: device/browser/region/cohort, and model variant breakdown
- Structured signal ingestion: policy hits, hallucination classifier scores, user-flag counts

Automation helpers (todo list for infra team)
- Console button to create HC-Canary: collects metadata, wires alerting, and publishes Slack msg with approval actions (approve/abort)
- Small script to collect 200 real examples from pilot and anonymize PII for human review
- Auto-generated short report (1p) summarizing key metrics at gate time

Private deployment caveats
- For private (VPC/on-prem) customers, human checkpoint may be performed by customer security/compliance reps using the same signoff protocol. Ensure playbook includes an exportable artifact and minimal data sharing (hashed inputs where necessary).
- Rollback paths in private deployments are often slower (coord with account infra). Plan longer guard windows.

Checklist for publishing the HC-Canary artifacts
- Short outcome doc (1 page) uploaded to experiment folder
- Dashboard snapshot and raw metric export stored in experiment folder
- Prompts and failing examples (anonymized) attached
- Linked JIRA for follow-ups and PRs

Notes-to-self / open questions
- Should we require a red-team run for any experiment touching the safety tag? Might add too much friction—maybe thresholded by risk score.
- How to encode stake-weighted approvals for large orgs? (e.g., for high-regulated accounts require compliance sign-off)
- Possibility: a ‘fast-approve’ rotation where a designated HGA can approve experiments <2% and <1h expected exposure.

Quick template (copy-paste) for the HC Slack notification
- [HC-CANARY] {experiment_id} ready for human gate approval
- Owner: {owner}
- Pilot duration: {pilot_dur}  — current signals: latency {p95_delta}, errors {err_delta}, safety_hits {count}
- Approve: :white_check_mark:  Abort: :no_entry:  (Reactions will trigger action)

Appendix: minimal example of experiment metadata (single-line)
- id: console/25q1/structured-answers-rewrite | baseline: rw-v2.1 | candidate: rw-v2.2-augmented | slice: us-east-low-risk | initial: 2% | gate: human | signals: safety,latency,quality

End of doc — this is a working draft. Please add comments inline or append runbook step if you own automation tasks.
